items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: when he wanted some lyrics and put Sarah Vaughan on it, good

ctx.x: And he wanted the prestige in it. That's what he wanted. And I followed that, and I thought BOUGHT that. But what he did, he come to me, and they wanted Sarah to do Dutch Kitchen BOUNCE and have somebody to do the lyrics on it to the title, to the melody. But he wanted to publishing company bring me in and let another publisher come in and handle it, and I said, 'No, indeed. I am the controller of this one. I've been through this already with Lionel Hampton with 'Tempo and Swing.' I don't want nobody to have none…

too soon, when it got to go that way.
And that's where I drew the line. I went along with Bob on what he wanted, but when he wanted some lyrics and put Sarah Vaughan on it, good, but let me still control it with Wayne Music Publishing Company. That's mine. But he wanted Mills or somebody downtown in New York. No way. No way. I've been ripped off too much, and I'm tired of being ripped off. I'd take it and let it die before I'd let somebody make more money off of my own material than I could make off of it, and…
